2026-09-12T20:37:15.8930175Z To create a pull request:
2026-09-12T20:37:15.8930741Z 1. Make any file changes directly in the working directory.
2026-09-12T20:37:15.8932062Z 2. If you haven't done so already, create a new local branch using `git checkout -b <branch-name>` with an appropriate unique name.
2026-09-12T20:37:15.8994644Z 3. Add and commit your changes to the branch. Be careful to add exactly the files you intend, and check there are no extra files left un-added. Verify you haven't deleted or changed any files you didn't intend to.
2026-09-12T20:37:15.8996629Z 4. Do not push your changes. That will be done by the tool.
2026-09-12T20:37:15.8997851Z 5. Create the pull request with the create_pull_request tool from safeoutputs exactly once, only when the final title/body/branch are ready.
2026-09-12T20:37:15.8999566Z 6. After calling `create_pull_request`, STOP. Do not probe with another PR call, do not test auth with manual `git push`, and do not rewrite git remotes.
2026-09-12T20:37:15.9000532Z

2026-09-12T20:37:15.9020230Z 
2026-09-12T20:37:15.9020696Z For multiple or complex arguments, pipe a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel:
2026-09-12T20:37:15.9021512Z ```bash
2026-09-12T20:37:15.9022115Z printf '{"item_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody."}' | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-09-12T20:37:15.9023030Z # or write to a file: safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-09-12T20:37:15.9023883Z ```
2026-09-12T20:37:15.9024084Z 
2026-09-12T20:37:15.9027179Z **Multi-line or long `body` content:** do NOT build the JSON payload with `printf`/`echo` embedding raw newlines or many escaped characters directly in the command line — the sandbox's shell command-injection guard may reject long or complex quoted arguments (reporting "expansion patterns"/"command substitution" even though none are present) and retrying the identical command will fail again. Instead, write the content to a temp file with a heredoc, then use `jq -Rs` to inject it as the `body` field:
2026-09-12T20:37:15.9030383Z ```bash
2026-09-12T20:37:15.9030784Z cat <<'EOF' > /tmp/gh-aw/body.md
2026-09-12T20:37:15.9031267Z Title
2026-09-12T20:37:15.9031477Z 
2026-09-12T20:37:15.9031676Z Multi-line body content goes here.
2026-09-12T20:37:15.9032168Z EOF
2026-09-12T20:37:15.9032892Z jq -Rs '{title: "My title", body: .}' /tmp/gh-aw/body.md | safeoutputs create_discussion .
2026-09-12T20:37:15.9033826Z ```
2026-09-12T20:37:15.9034931Z If a shell command is rejected for containing expansion patterns, do not retry the same command — switch to the heredoc + `jq -Rs` pattern above.
2026-09-12T20:37:15.9035895Z 
2026-09-12T20:37:15.9036509Z To inject an entire local file as the `body` field without re-embedding its content in the model context, use `jq -Rs`:

2026-09-12T20:37:15.9089061Z 
2026-09-12T20:37:15.9089535Z A single self-contained HTML file (inline CSS and vanilla JS, no external resources) with:
2026-09-12T20:37:15.9090181Z 
2026-09-12T20:37:15.9090614Z - Title, UTC generation time, release count, and a link to the official releases page.
2026-09-12T20:37:15.9091665Z - One card per release: name or tag, UTC date, stable/prerelease badge, short highlights
2026-09-12T20:37:15.9092754Z - Search, an all/stable/prerelease filter, and a visible result count.
2026-09-12T20:37:15.9093871Z - Light/dark themes, accessible markup, and an empty state if there are no releases.
2026-09-12T20:37:15.9095604Z - Render every release card directly in the HTML so the releases remain visible if JavaScript is disabled or fails. Use JavaScript only as progressive enhancement for search, filters, counts, and themes.
2026-09-12T20:37:15.9096883Z 
2026-09-12T20:37:15.9097462Z Summarize only what the notes say, keeping qualifiers like preview, platform limits, and security impact.
